book.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
book.author: Yuval Noah Harari

confidence_note: Based on chapter summaries of chapter 5, not the book text. Omitted: forager working hours (4-6 h in old text, unsupported), verbatim 'slaves to wheat' quote, animal domestication. Year 2011 is the Hebrew first edition.
facts: Chapter 5 is titled 'History's Biggest Fraud'; the fraud is the Agricultural Revolution.
The average farmer worked harder than the average forager and got a worse diet.
About 10,000 years ago wheat was a wild grass in a small part of the Middle East; within a few millennia it grew worldwide. Harari says wheat domesticated humans.
Farm work: clearing stones, weeding, guarding against worms and blight, fences, irrigation canals, dung; linked to slipped discs, arthritis, hernias.
Humans are omnivores; grains were a small share before farming; a cereal diet is poor in minerals and vitamins; reliance on few crops meant a failed harvest could kill thousands or millions.
An area feeding 100 healthy foragers could support a village of 1,000, with disease and malnutrition; in most farming societies at least one child in three died before 20.
Luxury trap: harder work seemed to secure children's food; larger families, disease, theft and walls followed; change was gradual; luxuries become necessities and obligations.
Company analogy: a species' success is measured in DNA copies as a company's is in money, not employee happiness.
Not everyone accepts the argument; at least one reviewer calls the evidence questionable.
scene_details: wild grass in a small corner of the Middle East
clearing stones, weeding, digging irrigation canals, spreading dung
a village of 1,000 on land that fed 100 foragers
tension: A shift told as progress left the typical farmer working harder, eating worse and less secure, yet it spread.
opening_idea: Start from the wild grass or the farm tasks and who really served whom.

lessons.idea: Write down what a convenience will cost before it becomes normal.
lessons.anchor: the luxury trap: luxuries become necessities and obligations

reflect_final: Which recent convenience took more of your time or attention than you expected?

use_cases.move: Link to the farmers' sensible calculation and write down a normal week with the thing.

use_cases.situation: Someone at home says it will make life easier

pocket_idea: Wheat domesticated its farmers; list what a convenience will ask of you before you accept it.
